The quantitative clause (6.24) is faithful as MeanClass over the main-chain strip, BaseContextAssembly.nativeStrip, which equals ActualInitialMean.strip and geometry.strip. That strip fixes ε = Q^h, S = max(1,ℓ²), the flat ζ and a comparable δ, and differentiates in R. S_α (6.25) is UnweightedClass over localSlowStripData. The class itself omits torus descent, smooth zero extension and the (6.20) compatibility. These appear only as separate predicates (MovingField, PeriodicOn, overlap StateOn), which the cycle invariant carries alongside. So Lean's M_α is strictly larger, and the verdict is DELTA, partial. The auditor's secondary findings, that no strip fixes every datum and that the lifted S_α encoding is weaker, are refuted by both skeptics, and I confirmed this in the source.

findings.summary: The Lean mean class MeanClass states only smoothness on the open strip and the (6.24) bounds, so alone it does not imply torus periodicity. Periodicity and vanishing off the shell are a separate predicate, MovingField; band-chart compatibility is StateOn. No single predicate bundles them.

The auditor claimed no single Lean strip fixes every datum of (6.23)/(6.24). That is false. nativeStrip, which is ActualInitialMean.strip and geometry.strip, fixes ε = Q^h, S = max(1,ℓ²), the flat ζ and the log δ, and differentiates in physical R.

The auditor claimed UnweightedClass(logStripData) in meanClass_pressureMass_lift is weaker than S_α. It is not. The function is constant in x.1 and Y, so evaluating at x.1 = √(ab), where δ is a fixed constant, and composing with insertSlow gives exactly (6.25).

On the actual strip the shell variable is r = R/√q̃ = √(2X), not X. Hence a_a = 4cL = edgeExponent, a_b = 4, δ_Lean = min(1, ½log(X/X_a), ½log(X_b/X)) ∈ [δ/2, δ], and S = max(1, ℓ²). All of these are equivalent up to constants.
